statement: Attainment is equivalent to a compatible finite urn reaching the optimized binomial height.

statement: Attainment is equivalent to a compatible finite urn reaching the optimized binomial height.
hypotheses_and_conclusion: {h : ℕ} (hh : 0 < h) (x : Fin h → ℕ) (m : ℕ) (hx : ∀ i, x i ≤ m) {p : ℝ} (hp : p ∈ Icc 0 1) (hmax : IsMaxOn (fun q ↦ ∏ i, binomialFace m (x i) q) (Icc 0 1) p) : let D := {v : ℕ × ℕ | v.1 ≤ v.2 ∧ m ≤ v.2 ∧ ∀ i, Compatible m v.2 v.1 (x i)} let L := fun v : ℕ × ℕ ↦ likelihood m v.2 v.1 x (∃ v ∈ D, IsMaxOn L D v) ↔ ∃ v ∈ D, (∏ i, binomialFace m (x i) p) ≤ L v
dossier_scope_note: All compatible marked-count-held samples. The finite prefix and residue algorithm remains open.

statement: The zero-stop branch is flat at one and the positive-stop branch tends to zero with growing population.
hypotheses_and_conclusion: {h m r : ℕ} (hh : 0 < h) (x : Fin h → ℕ) (hf : ∃ j, ∀ i, Compatible (m + j) m r (x i)) : (r = 0 ∧ (∀ i, x i = 0) ∧ ∀ j, totalLikelihood x (m + j) m r = 1) ∨ (0 < r ∧ Tendsto (fun j : ℕ ↦ totalLikelihood x (m + j) m r) atTop (𝓝 0))
dossier_scope_note: Population is the fixed marked count plus the unmarked count.

hypotheses_and_conclusion: {h : ℕ} (hh : 0 < h) (N m r c : ℕ) : (∀ A B C, totalLikelihood (fun _ : Fin h ↦ c) A B C ≤ totalLikelihood (fun _ : Fin h ↦ c) N m r) ↔ m ≤ N ∧ r ≤ m ∧ r = c ∧ (c = 0 ∨ m = N)
dossier_scope_note: Constant samples, including zero. The nonconstant fixed-stopping-count slice algorithm remains open.

statement: A compatible finite urn on positive samples wins exactly when it reaches the largest of finitely many stopping-count slice suprema.

dossier_scope_note: Slice suprema are defined order-theoretically. An effective finite computation of each slice is still open.

statement: Threshold ties give unbounded fitted collapse, positive excesses attain, and the unrestricted subuniform shape branch is unbounded.

dossier_scope_note: The reference branch uses finite interior log likelihood.

statement: There is attainment, with vanishing likelihood at nonuniform upper contact and at infinite shape for any positive excess.

dossier_scope_note: Includes the flat all-zero sample and closed uniform contact.

dossier_scope_note: The reference chart explicitly gives compatible upper contacts infinite log likelihood.

statement: Fixed-shape constant collapse and negative-exponent collapse diverge, critical collapse is finite and unattained, and the unrestricted subuniform interior is unbounded.

dossier_scope_note: The critical bound ranges over every finite location and scale.

statement: Held scale always gives a finite optimum. An infinite-shape path with likelihood bounded below requires constant data and location converging to the common value.
hypotheses_and_conclusion: {n : ℕ} (hn : 0 < n) (x : Fin n → ℝ) {s : ℝ} (hs : 0 < s) : (∃ m ξ, ξ ∈ shapeDomain (fun i ↦ x i - m) s ∧ ∀ q κ, κ ∈ shapeDomain (fun i ↦ x i - q) s → logLik (fun i ↦ x i - q) s κ ≤ logLik (fun i ↦ x i - m) s ξ) ∧ (∀ (m ξ : ℕ → ℝ) (B : ℝ), (∀ᶠ t in atTop, ξ t ∈ shapeDomain (fun i ↦ x i - m t) s) → Tendsto ξ atTop atTop → (∀ᶠ t in atTop, B ≤ logLik (fun i ↦ x i - m t) s (ξ t)) → ∃ M, (∀ i, x i = M) ∧ Tendsto m atTop (𝓝 M))
dossier_scope_note: The positive trace necessity covers arbitrary compatible sequences.

statement: On constant data a finite limit of the scaled location gap gives the explicit infinite-shape log likelihood trace.

dossier_scope_note: Finite scaled-gap limits at held positive scale.

statement: The complete argmax on uniform-feasible data consists of the uniform location interval and the constant sample ridge.
hypotheses_and_conclusion: {n : ℕ} (x : Fin n → ℝ) {s : ℝ} (hs : 0 < s) {i j : Fin n} (hi : ∀ k, x i ≤ x k) (hj : ∀ k, x k ≤ x j) (hspan : x j - x i ≤ s) : let D := {p : ℝ × ℝ | p.2 ∈ shapeDomain (fun k ↦ x k - p.1) s} let L := fun p : ℝ × ℝ ↦ logLik (fun k ↦ x k - p.1) s p.2 ∀ p, (p ∈ D ∧ IsMaxOn L D p) ↔ (p.2 = -1 ∧ p.1 ∈ Icc (x j - s) (x i)) ∨ (-1 ≤ p.2 ∧ p.1 = x i ∧ x i = x j)
dossier_scope_note: The nonuniform singleton for span above scale remains open.

statement: With valid endpoints the mode interval is compact and the positive-likelihood compatibility test is exact.
hypotheses_and_conclusion: {n : ℕ} (hn : 0 < n) (x : Fin n → ℝ) {a b : ℝ} (hab : a < b) : let D := Icc a b let L := fun c ↦ supportLikelihood x (a, b, c) let compatible := (∀ i, x i ∈ D) ∧ ¬ ((∃ i, x i = a) ∧ (∃ i, x i = b)) IsCompact D ∧ ((∃ c ∈ D, IsMaxOn L D c ∧ 0 < L c) ↔ compatible) ∧ (¬ compatible → ∀ c ∈ D, L c = 0)
dossier_scope_note: The compatibility predicate models the mathematical condition used by the API.

dossier_scope_note: The two-level count comparison and count-stratum nullity remain open.

statement: On positive excesses, the almost-everywhere and pointwise two-level uniqueness hold, with a two-winner example at threshold zero.
hypotheses_and_conclusion: (μ : ℝ) : (∀ {n : ℕ} (w : Fin n → ℕ), (∀ i, 0 < w i) → ∀ᵐ x : Fin n → ℝ ∂volume, (∃ i j, x i ≠ x j) → ∀ p q, UniqueAE.Winner (AE2Lomax.domain μ) (AE2Lomax.likelihood (1) μ w) x p → UniqueAE.Winner (AE2Lomax.domain μ) (AE2Lomax.likelihood (1) μ w) x q → p = q) ∧ (∀ {n : ℕ}, 0 < n → ∀ x : Fin n → ℝ, (∀ i, μ < x i) → (∃ a b : ℝ, ∀ i, x i = a ∨ x i = b) → let L := fun v : ℝ × ℝ ↦ Transfer.ParetoII.logLik x μ v.1 v.2 (∃ v ∈ Lomax.domain, IsMaxOn L Lomax.domain v) → ∃! v, v ∈ Lomax.domain ∧ IsMaxOn L Lomax.domain v) ∧ ( ∃ a ∈ Ioo ((2 : ℝ) ^ 512)⁻¹ ((2 : ℝ) ^ 32)⁻¹, let x : Fin 21 → ℝ := fun i ↦ if i.val = 0 then a else if i.val ≤ 10 then 1 else 100 (∀ i, 0 < x i) ∧ ∃ p q : ℝ × ℝ, p.2 < q.2 ∧ {v ∈ Lomax.domain | IsMaxOn (fun b : ℝ × ℝ ↦ Transfer.ParetoII.logLik x 0 b.1 b.2) Lomax.domain v} = {p, q} ∧ Transfer.ParetoII.bestShiftedExp x 0 < Transfer.ParetoII.logLik x 0 q.1 q.2)
dossier_scope_note: The almost-everywhere branch uses the inverse-scale coordinate.

hypotheses_and_conclusion: : (∀ {n : ℕ} (w : Fin n → ℕ), (∀ i, 0 < w i) → ∀ᵐ x : Fin n → ℝ ∂volume, (∃ i j, x i ≠ x j) → ∀ p q, UniqueAE.Winner (AE2Lomax.domain 0) (AE2Lomax.likelihood (1) 0 w) x p → UniqueAE.Winner (AE2Lomax.domain 0) (AE2Lomax.likelihood (1) 0 w) x q → p = q) ∧ (∀ {n : ℕ}, 0 < n → ∀ x : Fin n → ℝ, (∀ i, 0 < x i) → (∃ a b : ℝ, ∀ i, x i = a ∨ x i = b) → let L := fun v : ℝ × ℝ ↦ Lomax.logLik x v.1 v.2 (∃ v ∈ Lomax.domain, IsMaxOn L Lomax.domain v) → ∃! v, v ∈ Lomax.domain ∧ IsMaxOn L Lomax.domain v) ∧ ( ∃! a, a ∈ Ioo ((2 : ℝ) ^ 512)⁻¹ ((2 : ℝ) ^ 32)⁻¹ ∧ let x : Fin 21 → ℝ := fun i ↦ if i.val = 0 then a else if i.val ≤ 10 then 1 else 100 ∃ p ∈ Lomax.domain, ∃ q ∈ Lomax.domain, p.2 < 1024 ∧ 1024 < q.2 ∧ IsMaxOn (fun v : ℝ × ℝ ↦ Lomax.logLik x v.1 v.2) Lomax.domain p ∧ IsMaxOn (fun v : ℝ × ℝ ↦ Lomax.logLik x v.1 v.2) Lomax.domain q ∧ (∀ b ∈ Lomax.domain, IsMaxOn (fun v : ℝ × ℝ ↦ Lomax.logLik x v.1 v.2) Lomax.domain b → b = p ∨ b = q) ∧ Lomax.bestExp x < Lomax.logLik x p.1 p.2)

statement: Count strata have almost-everywhere uniqueness, attained two-level samples have a unique fit, and a positive sample has exactly two winners.
hypotheses_and_conclusion: : (∀ {n : ℕ} (w : Fin n → ℕ), (∀ i, 0 < w i) → ∀ᵐ x : Fin n → ℝ ∂volume, (∃ i j, x i ≠ x j) → ∀ p q, UniqueAE.Winner (AE2Lomax.domain 0) (AE2Lomax.likelihood (-1) 0 w) x p → UniqueAE.Winner (AE2Lomax.domain 0) (AE2Lomax.likelihood (-1) 0 w) x q → p = q) ∧ (∀ {n : ℕ}, 0 < n → ∀ x : Fin n → ℝ, (∀ i, 0 < x i) → (∃ a b : ℝ, ∀ i, x i = a ∨ x i = b) → let L := fun v : ℝ × ℝ ↦ Transfer.InvPareto.logLik x v.1 v.2 (∃ v ∈ Lomax.domain, IsMaxOn L Lomax.domain v) → ∃! v, v ∈ Lomax.domain ∧ IsMaxOn L Lomax.domain v) ∧ ( ∃ a ∈ Ioo ((2 : ℝ) ^ 512)⁻¹ ((2 : ℝ) ^ 32)⁻¹, let x : Fin 21 → ℝ := fun i ↦ (if i.val = 0 then a else if i.val ≤ 10 then 1 else 100)⁻¹ (∀ i, 0 < x i) ∧ ∃ p q : ℝ × ℝ, p.2 < q.2 ∧ {v ∈ Lomax.domain | IsMaxOn (fun b : ℝ × ℝ ↦ Transfer.InvPareto.logLik x b.1 b.2) Lomax.domain v} = {p, q} ∧ Transfer.InvPareto.bestInvExp x < Transfer.InvPareto.logLik x p.1 p.2)
dossier_scope_note: The almost-everywhere branch uses reciprocal coordinates in the likelihood.

dossier_scope_note: The nonconstant adjacent-ratio comparison, adjacency, and prime-power exclusion remain open.

dossier_scope_note: The family-specific analytic profile, score confinement and trace criterion remain open.

statement: The Poisson supporting inequality gives a strict finite-rate bound for all positive index shifts.

dossier_scope_note: Analytic step in the one-sided supporting test.

statement: For nonnegative counts of positive mean passing the Poisson supporting test, the maximum is unique at the Poisson face.
hypotheses_and_conclusion: {n : ℕ} (hn : 0 < n) (x : Fin n → ℕ) {d : ℝ} (hd : 0 < d) (hmean : d = (∑ i, (x i : ℝ)) / n) (hs : ∀ t ≥ 0, (∑ i, poissonMass t (x i) / ((n : ℝ) * poissonMass d (x i))) ≤ 1) : let y : Fin n → ℤ := fun i ↦ x i (d, 0) ∈ domain ∧ IsMaxOn (likelihood y) domain (d, 0) ∧ ∀ p ∈ domain, IsMaxOn (likelihood y) domain p → p = (d, 0)
dossier_scope_note: Nonnegative orientation and positive mean.

statement: For nonpositive counts of negative mean passing the reflected supporting test, the maximum is unique at the reflected Poisson face.
hypotheses_and_conclusion: {n : ℕ} (hn : 0 < n) (x : Fin n → ℕ) {d : ℝ} (hd : 0 < d) (hmean : d = (∑ i, (x i : ℝ)) / n) (hs : ∀ t ≥ 0, (∑ i, poissonMass t (x i) / ((n : ℝ) * poissonMass d (x i))) ≤ 1) : let y : Fin n → ℤ := fun i ↦ -(x i : ℤ) (0, d) ∈ domain ∧ IsMaxOn (likelihood y) domain (0, d) ∧ ∀ p ∈ domain, IsMaxOn (likelihood y) domain p → p = (0, d)
dossier_scope_note: Nonpositive orientation and strictly negative signed mean.

hypotheses_and_conclusion: {n : ℕ} (hn : 0 < n) (x : Fin n → ℕ) {j : ℕ} (hx : ∀ i, x i = j ∨ x i = j + 1) {d : ℝ} (hd : 0 < d) (hmean : d = (∑ i, (x i : ℝ)) / n) : ∀ t ≥ 0, (∑ i, poissonMass t (x i) / ((n : ℝ) * poissonMass d (x i))) ≤ 1
